title: dBud rtsi tshad 'joms sogs
shelf_note: A Sowa Rigpa (Tibetan medicine) bundle on heat and contagious fevers ('Thousand Doses of Jewels', 'Sunlight Garland', a text on 'the basis of confusion' by an ācārya). It belongs in a Gangtey Monastery holding; the tradition label is the collection stratum, not a subject.
structure_note: Every image shows two loose leaves of khyug-yig (cursive dbu med) with dense interlinear notes. The OCR marks each seam with <leaf-break/> and the translator keeps the leaves apart. The book record says pages_ocr 31, but the structure counts give OCR on 115/115 page records; 27/115 are translated. Several works are bound under one title (new yig-mgo and invocations on pp.45 and 86), as the 'sogs' in the title allows.

tr_errors.problem: an invented gloss lists the wrong drugs for the Six Excellent Ones (the standard six are bamboo pith, saffron, clove, nutmeg, small and large cardamom; cubeb and sandalwood are not among them), so a reader gets a wrong formula

tr_errors.problem: interlinear gloss dropped in translation

book_verdict: The right leaves, transcribed coherently from difficult cursive with interlinear notes; the English reads well. It invents in places: a physician's name, an epithet, a named fever stage, and a wrong list of the 'Six Excellent' drugs in a gloss.
reader_summary: A bundle of Tibetan medical verse treatises on heat and contagious fevers, copied in cursive script with interlinear notes. The transcription is of the right leaves but cannot be checked word by word from the cursive, and it drops many of the notes. The English is a usable guide to the argument, but the drug glosses and some proper names are made up and should not be trusted for formulas.

title: rTa mgrin dpa' bo gcig pa
shelf_note: A Nyingma ritual compilation from a Gangtey holding. The pages read are a mandala-drawing manual, an empowerment liturgy with skull-cups, banners and phur pas, a Vajravidāraṇa sādhana, and a Guru Thod phreng rtsal feast liturgy. None of them is visibly the Hayagrīva text named in the title.
structure_note: A composite volume: the title names one Hayagrīva practice, but the sampled pages are other works, so the title describes at most the first item. Each image holds two or three leaves; on p.94 a loose cursive slip sits above two leaves, with no <leaf-break/> between the slip and the first leaf. printed_backsteps 1 and printed_repeats 1 are on only 7 printed numbers in 270 records, most likely misread margin numerals, not a reordering. 86/270 translated.

tr_errors.problem: wrong gloss: the name means 'Vajra Destroyer', not 'subduer of vajras'

tr_errors.problem: seam fragment rendered as a sentence, and 'Recite' added

book_verdict: Clean dbu can liturgical leaves (pp.132, 188, 254) are transcribed well and mostly translated well, though p.188 gives the deities 'eighty-five arms'. The cursive slip on p.94 is transcribed unreliably and translated into fluent nonsense, under an invented '94 (Front)' label.
reader_summary: A Nyingma ritual compilation: empowerment and feast liturgies, a Vajravidāraṇa sādhana and a mandala-drawing manual, bound under a Hayagrīva title that does not describe the sampled pages. The block-letter leaves are transcribed accurately, and the English of the liturgies is faithful enough to follow. Loose cursive slips are not, and the iconographic details need checking against the Tibetan.

title: rTsa rgyud rdo rje gzhon nu (EAP039-1-4-226)
shelf_note: Pema Lingpa's Vajrakīla (rDo rje gzhon nu) treasure cycle: a commentary on the root tantra, the Phur pa srog gi spu gri history and dances, and a Tsogyal–Padmasambhava dialogue on māras. It suits a Bhutanese monastic holding such as Gangtey.
structure_note: Each image holds three leaves (rectos), each with a <leaf-break/> except where a leaf is a title leaf: on p.79 the third leaf is the title leaf of a new work (…phur ba'i sgrub thabs bzhugs so), and the OCR leaves it out. Several works are bound under the root-tantra title. 70/128 translated (book field pages_ocr 72, but OCR on all 128 records).

ocr_errors.problem: the blank after the yig-mgo is rendered as a run of 17 shad

tr_errors.english: regarding the timing of the equinox … at the midpoint of the night
tr_errors.problem: 'equinox' added alongside the correct 'midpoint of the night'

ocr_errors.image: third leaf: a framed title leaf, ༔ སྙིང་ཐིག་ཡང་གསང་རྡོ་རྗེ་ཕུར་བའི་སྒྲུབ་ཐབས་བཞུགས་སོ ༔ (approx.)
ocr_errors.problem: the title leaf of the next work is not transcribed, so the reader is not told that a new work begins

ocr_errors.image: folio labels in the left margins of each leaf

tr_errors.english: for six periods of ten days
tr_errors.problem: the retreat length is six periods of thirty days (gsum bcu = thirty); the English drops 'three' and gives sixty days instead of 180

ocr_errors.problem: 'chams (ritual dance) misread as 'tshams throughout the list of dances

tr_errors.english: The movement-boundary for the peaceful. The posture-boundary for the increasing.
tr_errors.problem: the cham dances of the Phur pa cycle become 'boundaries' throughout (a misread carried into fluent English); 'Life-force Boundary' should be the life-force dance

tr_errors.english: If they do not cause me to be subdued <note>by pride or distraction</note>
tr_errors.problem: unclear sense padded with a speculative note

book_verdict: Careful dbu can leaves, very well transcribed apart from a consistent 'chams→'tshams misread. The translation is fluent and mostly faithful, but it states the retreat length wrongly (sixty days for 180), and the OCR skips a title leaf.
reader_summary: Texts from Pema Lingpa's Vajrakīla treasure cycle: a commentary on the root tantra, the history and ritual dances of the 'Life-force Razor' Phurba, and Tsogyal's questions on obstacles. The transcription is of the right leaves and largely accurate. The English follows the argument well, but numbers and technical terms (dances read as 'boundaries') should be checked against the Tibetan.

title: bKa' 'khor bar pai dkar chag nong ston gsung
shelf_note: A Gangtey Monastery manuscript bundle. The pages read are dhāraṇī sūtras for protection (Indra and the asuras, hail and nāga rites), the dedication verses of Bodhicaryāvatāra ch. 10, and a Dzogchen Nyingthig anthology of tantra quotations.
structure_note: The title names a catalogue (dkar chag) by Nong ston, but none of the four sampled pages is a catalogue: this is a miscellany, and the title probably describes only the first item. On p.127 the third leaf is a title leaf of a new work with no <leaf-break/>, so its title is fused onto the end of the prayer leaf. printed_backsteps 3 and printed_repeats 3 (on 10 printed numbers) fit a bundle of several works, each restarting its foliation, rather than a misorder. 30/202 translated.

tr_errors.problem: rig sngags (vidyā-mantra) taken as vidyādhara and glossed accordingly

tr_errors.problem: 'sons' rendered 'daughters'

ocr_errors.image: the last line is a separate framed title leaf (red-ruled), roughly གདམས་ངག་…འཕོ་བའི་…བཞུགས་སོ
ocr_errors.problem: title leaf fused to the prayer leaf with no seam

tr_errors.problem: the title of a new ('pho ba) work, 'herein is contained', is presented as the colophon of the preceding prayer and rendered 'is complete'

book_verdict: Clear, accurate transcription of dbu med and dbu can leaves, and a faithful English of dhāraṇīs, the Bodhicaryāvatāra dedication and Dzogchen quotations. The title promises a catalogue that these pages are not, and one title leaf is read as a colophon.
reader_summary: A miscellany bound under the title of a Kangyur catalogue: protective dhāraṇī sūtras, the dedication chapter of the Bodhicaryāvatāra, and a Great Perfection anthology of tantra citations. The transcription is of the right leaves and reads accurately. The English can be trusted for the sense, with small slips in names, and the reader should know the title does not describe the contents.
